items.title: Gecko Robotics secures $300M contract with the U.S. Navy
items.summary: Gecko Robotics secured an additional $300 million contract with the U.S. Navy and GSA. This increase quadruples the ceiling value of the contract to improve fleet readiness and reduce maintenance delays. The company's AI and robotic technology, including the Komodo system, identifies structural issues up to 50 times faster than traditional methods. This technology allows for damage assessment without stripping deck coatings, saving the Navy significant repair costs. The expanded contract supports the Navy's goal of achieving 80% fleet readiness by accelerating inspections.

The company's artificial intelligence and robotic technology, specifically the Komodo system, is utilized to identify structural issues up to fifty times faster than conventional assessment methods. This capability enables damage assessment without the need for stripping deck coatings, resulting in significant cost savings for the Navy during repairs. The expanded contract directly supports the Navy's objective of reaching eighty percent fleet readiness through the acceleration of inspection processes. This development signals increased adoption of advanced robotics in maritime infrastructure inspection.

items.title: ¡Llegamos a Madrid! Waymo is coming to Spain
items.summary: Waymo is initiating the deployment of its fully autonomous ride-hailing service in Spain, starting with the Region of Madrid. The company plans to welcome its first riders in 2027, beginning with a phased, safety-first approach involving manual driving validation first. Waymo is collaborating with Spanish authorities and investing in local operations to align with regional and national safety goals. Data indicates that Waymo Driver has been involved in 95% fewer crashes involving serious injury or worse than human drivers. The autonomous technology aims to enhance urban mobility by reducing accidents caused by human error.
items.audio_script: From Waymo Blog, "¡Llegamos a Madrid! Waymo is coming to Spain". Waymo plans to introduce its service to riders in 2027 through a phased approach that prioritizes safety, beginning with manual driving validation. The company is actively collaborating with Spanish authorities and investing in local operations to ensure alignment with regional and national safety objectives. Data from Waymo Driver indicates that the autonomous technology has been involved in ninety-five percent fewer crashes involving serious injury or worse than human drivers, aiming to improve urban mobility by mitigating accidents resulting from human error. This development signals a step toward integrating advanced autonomous technology into public transportation networks across the continent.

items.title: Agility Robotics’ new Digit humanoid to work 20 hours a day with Nyobolt fast-charging battery
items.summary: Agility Robotics partnered with Nyobolt to upgrade its Digit 5 humanoid robot with a fast-charging battery system. This technology enables Digit 5 to work over 20 hours daily, improving uptime and operational economics. The new battery system allows for a 90-minute runtime with a 9-minute charge, achieving a 10:1 run-to-charge ratio. This innovation addresses power limitations that previously constrained autonomous robot fleet economics. The enhanced battery performance is designed to boost the value proposition of Digit 5 for warehouse and manufacturing operations.

The new battery technology facilitates a nine-minute charge for a ninety-minute runtime, establishing a ten to one run-to-charge ratio. This advancement directly addresses previous power limitations that restricted the economics of autonomous robot fleets in warehouse and manufacturing settings. The enhanced battery performance is projected to increase the value proposition of the Digit 5 platform for industrial applications. This development signals a step forward in improving the practical viability of autonomous robotics in commercial environments.

items.title: The Robot I Didn’t Expect to Build
items.summary: Agility Robotics launched Digit 5, the first humanoid robot designed for safe and economic work at scale in warehouses. Digit 5 is engineered to lift 23-kilogram bins and can operate safely near human coworkers using proximity sensors. The development of Digit 5 involved prioritizing customer needs and safety regulations over the original vision of a purely graceful design. This resulted in a larger, more functional robot that balances commercial viability with achieving the ultimate goal of human-like motion. Ultimately, Digit 5 serves as a practical foundation for pursuing the longer-term vision of fully agile and dexterous humanoid robots.
items.audio_script: From IEEE Spectrum - Robotics, "The Robot I Didn’t Expect to Build". The development process prioritized customer needs and safety regulations over an initial purely graceful design, resulting in a larger, more functional robot that balances commercial viability with the pursuit of human-like motion. This engineering approach established a practical foundation for future advancements in fully agile and dexterous humanoid robotics. The successful deployment of Digit 5 indicates a tangible step toward applying advanced robotics in industrial settings.

items.title: Laplace Intelligence red-teams robots and self-driving cars before they hit the real world
items.summary: Laplace Intelligence builds automated red-teaming systems to stress-test physical AI for robotics and self-driving cars before real-world deployment. The company uses high-fidelity simulations, grounded in real-world data, with AI agents actively probing for failure points. Their method involves using AI to design corner cases by analyzing real-world data like news and police reports to challenge autonomous systems. This approach aims to create a shared foundation of evidence for safety and build trust among customers, insurers, and regulators. Laplace seeks to establish a "dynamic interactive testing process" as a new paradigm for physical AI safety.
items.audio_script: From TechCrunch - Robotics, "Laplace Intelligence red-teams robots and self-driving cars before they hit the real world". This report details how the company utilizes automated red-teaming systems to stress-test physical artificial intelligence for robotics and autonomous vehicles prior to actual deployment. The methodology involves constructing high-fidelity simulations grounded in real-world data, employing AI agents to actively probe for potential failure points. These agents use real-world data, such as news and police reports, to design challenging corner cases, thereby stress-testing autonomous systems. This process seeks to establish a shared foundation of evidence regarding safety and foster greater trust among stakeholders. Laplace is developing a dynamic interactive testing process as a new framework for physical AI safety. This development establishes a rigorous testing paradigm for ensuring the safety of autonomous physical systems entering the market.

items.title: Automation Created a Training Problem: Upskilling the Industrial Workforce
items.summary: Automation creates a skills gap because the need for new skills often outpaces training availability. Workers need new competencies, such as operating, maintaining, and programming automated systems, which are not covered by traditional training. Digital e-learning is effective for delivering knowledge across shift-based workforces, though hands-on practice remains essential for practical competence. Successful upskilling requires integrating training planning directly into the automation project timeline. Manufacturers must treat workforce upskilling as an operational priority, budgeted alongside hardware, to realize the full productivity gains of automation.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, "Automation Created a Training Problem: Upskilling the Industrial Workforce". This report details the skills gap created by automation, noting that the demand for new competencies frequently outpaces the availability of traditional training. The necessity for workers to acquire skills in operating, maintaining, and programming automated systems is not adequately addressed by current training structures. Digital e-learning methods are proving effective for disseminating knowledge among shift-based workforces, although practical, hands-on practice is still considered essential for achieving full competence. Successful workforce upskilling mandates the direct integration of training planning within the automation project timeline. Manufacturers must prioritize workforce development by budgeting it alongside hardware to ensure the realization of automation productivity gains. This indicates that integrating continuous skills development is a prerequisite for maximizing the return on investment in technological automation.

items.title: Toyota Material Handling says digital twins can ‘halve autonomous forklift commissioning time’
items.summary: Toyota Material Handling is utilizing Nvidia simulation and digital twin technologies to accelerate the development and commissioning of autonomous forklifts. This simulation-first approach aims to reduce commissioning effort by up to 50 percent and shorten time-to-market by up to 40 percent. The process involves using Nvidia Omniverse and Isaac Sim to virtually test autonomous vehicle systems in simulated factory environments. Digital twins allow teams to test navigation, safety logic, and real-world interactions, enabling early issue resolution and reducing on-site adjustments. This method also incorporates machine vision using synthetic data to improve object detection for pallet handling systems.

The process utilizes Nvidia Omniverse and Isaac Sim to virtually test autonomous vehicle systems within simulated factory environments. Digital twins enable teams to test navigation, safety logic, and real-world interactions, facilitating early issue resolution and minimizing the need for on-site adjustments. Furthermore, the methodology incorporates machine vision using synthetic data to enhance object detection capabilities for pallet handling systems. This advancement demonstrates a method for drastically reducing the physical testing requirements in robotics deployment. The integration of simulation into hardware development sets a new benchmark for industrial automation timelines.

items.title: What robot builders overlook about cooling compact servo drives and controllers
items.summary: Compact robotic systems face complex thermal management challenges due to the proximity of multiple heat-generating electronic components with restricted airflow. Effective thermal design requires evaluating system-level performance based on actual operating conditions, including peak loads and duty cycles, rather than just component ratings. Heat sink selection should be based on a calculated thermal budget, considering the thermal interface and mounting surface quality. Forced-air cooling effectiveness is limited by internal restrictions, and the mechanical mounting interface significantly impacts heat transfer. Ultimately, reliable thermal management demands early collaboration between thermal, mechanical, and manufacturing teams to ensure practical and reliable solutions.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, "What robot builders overlook about cooling compact servo drives and controllers". Heat sink selection must be based on a calculated thermal budget, taking into account the thermal interface and mounting surface quality. Forced-air cooling effectiveness is constrained by internal restrictions, and the mechanical mounting interface directly influences heat transfer. Reliable thermal management requires early collaboration among thermal, mechanical, and manufacturing teams to achieve practical and dependable solutions. This emphasis on system-level thermal analysis is crucial for the advancement of compact robotics in the technology sector.

items.title: Kodama raises $7M to bring robotics to forestry
items.summary: Kodama raised $7 million to advance physical AI in the forestry industry, focusing on commercial deployments in the southeastern U.S. The company uses a hybrid approach combining supervised autonomy and teleoperation to enhance machine capabilities on job sites. Their technology has already enabled machines to move over 100,000 tons of timber in commercial logging operations. Kodama is integrating with existing Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) to leverage existing machine knowledge and build a data advantage. This data collection aims to improve on-site productivity and enhance safety for forestry workers.

items.title: ABB Robotics introduces two new high-performance robots for precision manufacturing
items.summary: ABB Robotics has introduced two new compact, high-performance robots, the IRB 1700 and IRB 1700ID. These robots offer up to 20 percent shorter cycle times than comparable models, improving productivity in precision manufacturing. They feature payloads from 6 kg to 12 kg, high precision repeatability of 0.03 mm, and joint speeds up to 700 degrees per second. The new robots also reduce operating costs with up to 15 percent lower power consumption and longer service intervals. These systems are suitable for demanding tasks like arc welding and new electronics applications.

items.title: New ASTM standard aims to test how robots perform in the real world
items.summary: ASTM International is developing a standard to measure manipulator and mobile manipulator task performance under controlled optical-signal degradation. This proposed method will quantify how degradation in optical information impacts a robot's ability to complete tasks in real-world conditions. Degradation from factors like changing light or interference can cause downstream machine-learning models to receive poorer information, potentially leading to task failure or safety risks. The standard aims to provide a repeatable way to test performance under stress, helping developers identify system limitations before deployment. This research supports responsible real-world deployment and UN Sustainable Development Goal #8.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, "New ASTM standard aims to test how robots perform in the real world". This report details the development of a new standard by ASTM International to measure the performance of robotic manipulators and mobile manipulators under conditions of controlled optical-signal degradation. The proposed methodology quantifies the impact of degraded optical information on a robot's task completion capabilities in simulated real-world settings. Degradation caused by factors such as fluctuating light or interference is examined to determine how it affects downstream machine-learning models and the potential for task failure or safety risks. This standard seeks to establish a repeatable method for testing performance under stress to identify system limitations prior to deployment, supporting responsible real-world integration and contributing to UN Sustainable Development Goal number eight. The development provides a framework for rigorously assessing robotic performance in complex environments.

items.title: Daimon Robotics building the infrastructure layer for tactile intelligence
items.summary: Daimon Robotics is building the infrastructure layer connecting tactile sensing, data collection, simulation, and AI models for tactile intelligence. The company aims to provide tools for other developers to build more capable robotic systems rather than developing a single foundation model itself. They develop a pipeline to process tactile feedback at 30 Hz, linking real-world data with simulations to bridge the sim-to-real gap. This infrastructure supports manipulation tasks requiring robots to react to physical contact, such as assembly and packaging. Ultimately, Daimon seeks to create a tactile-grounded world model that allows robots to reason about physical interactions beyond visual perception.

This infrastructure supports manipulation tasks that necessitate robots reacting to physical contact, including assembly and packaging. The objective is to create a tactile-grounded world model enabling robots to reason about physical interactions beyond visual perception. This work indicates a focus on creating a foundational layer for advanced robotic reasoning systems.

items.title: Tesollo robotic hand sales set to surpass 1,000 units in 2026
items.summary: Tesollo, a South Korean robotics company, anticipates exceeding 1,000 cumulative sales of its robotic hands and grippers by the end of 2026. This growth is driven by increasing demand in humanoid robotics, physical AI, and industrial automation for flexible end-effectors. The company has expanded its production facilities and manufacturing infrastructure to meet this growing global demand. Tesollo currently offers a portfolio of articulated hands ranging from one to five fingers, serving both research and industrial applications. The company plans to further strengthen its manufacturing capabilities and pursue a potential public listing in South Korea.

items.title: Schaeffler opens Taicang humanoid factory with six robots
items.summary: Schaeffler launched its Taicang Humanoid Lighthouse on October 20, 2026, deploying six humanoid robots on a joint module assembly line. The 7,500 square meter facility integrates robot component production, humanoid training, and industrial deployment. The robots perform tasks such as material handling, sorting, fitting, inspection, and packaging within the site. The factory offers six training scenarios and uses a digital twin system to link training with production validation. Schaeffler intends for the facility to serve as a collaboration platform for Chinese robotics companies.

items.title: SPD robot training pairs virtual practice with real demos
items.summary: SPD robot training utilizes simulated demonstrations to develop a dexterous bimanual policy for real tasks like Jenga. This method combines extensive virtual teleoperation with brief real teleoperated demonstrations to gather training data for two arms and two hands. Five individuals collected 75 hours of demonstrations in VR, involving a 56-DOF simulated system across various scenes and objects. The collected data was used to pretrain a 222 million parameter diffusion transformer policy before adapting it to real data. Simulation pretraining outperformed behavior cloning for these tasks, offering a practical signal for evaluating performance.
items.audio_script: From Humanoid.guide, "SPD robot training pairs virtual practice with real demos". This report details a method for developing dexterous bimanual policies in robots using simulated demonstrations combined with real-world data. Five individuals collected seventy-five hours of demonstrations within a five-six-degree-of-freedom simulated system across various scenes and objects, generating data for two arms and two hands. This data was used to pretrain a two-hundred-twenty-two-million-parameter diffusion transformer policy before adapting it to actual data. The simulation pretraining demonstrated superior performance compared to behavior cloning for these tasks, providing a tangible evaluation signal. This advancement suggests a more effective approach for training complex robotic manipulation skills in realistic environments.

items.title: Primepick brings NSF-certified robotic hot-meal kiosk to US market
items.summary: Primepick is expanding its NSF-certified, robotic hot-meal kiosk, MealMate, to new locations. The kiosk serves hot dishes in 5-7 minutes and is being deployed in hospitals, nursing homes, and new sites in Huntsville, Chicago, and Dallas. MealMate provides access to hot meals outside traditional foodservice hours without requiring on-site kitchen staff. The system utilizes robotic arms, specialized storage, and proprietary software for automated management and inventory. This marketplace model connects customers with meals from local restaurants and dark kitchens.
